messages:
Sam W.: heads-up — after the staged rollout at ~18:03 UTC we started getting a spike of 5xx from hosted API (api-router). Support hit: SUP-5412, customer DataSwell reporting high error rate + unexpected billing charges. 502/504s ~= 4% of traffic, p50 latency +600ms. tagging @oncall @jordan

opsbot: incident-alert: api-router: 502-rate: 4.3% (5m), error-p50-latency: +620ms, x-correlation errors up. linked: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd/api-router?orgId=1

Jordan L.: I'll take point. quick check — was the staged flag flip today the prefix_kv_cache_v2 rollout?

Sam W.: yes. small percentage of traffic (5%) routed to the new path in us-west1. We also rolled a tiny auth header sanitizer tweak in same deploy (header-truncation-fix). Might be related.

Maria R.: I'm seeing repeated downstream 401 from auth-service for requests that look fine upstream. sample log: ```ERROR auth: token-validate failed: header too long -> truncated header: "x-auth: eyJhbGciOiJI..."``` several of these coincide with 502 spikes at the router.

Lee C.: curious — KV cache change manipulates request routing (prefixing) and may impact header encoding on the router path. Could be header size or serialized meta growing. Also noticed billing meter logs show extra tokens counted for failed attempts (double-metering on retry).

Anna (support): data swell on call — their app noticed retries and duplicate billing entries for same call id. They've paused traffic but want ETA. ticket SUP-5412 updated.

Jordan L.: repro checklist for infra folks: 1) curl to api-router with long Authorization header 2) send with prefix flag enabled route header 3) observe 502/401 in auth-service and duplicate meter increments. Example reproducer: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer LONGTOKEN..." -H "X-Client-Id: dataswell" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}' -v```

Sam W.: proposal — pause staged rollout and revert prefix_kv_cache_v2 on gateway for us-west1. rollback window now? ops will run. @Lee can you confirm rollback command and expected disruption? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Lee C.: rollback plan: 1) flip config flag to previous stable: `config set routing.prefix_kv_cache_v2=false --env=us-west1 --target=staged` 2) drain in-flight new-route pods: `kubectl -n api router set evict --selector=route=kv_v2` 3) monitor 5xx and billing-meter metrics. Expected customer impact: none for customers already paused, <1% increased latency for a minute during drain. I'm ready to run.

Jordan L.: I'll coordinate with on-call to execute. tagging @opsbot to create a rollback runbook entry. Also need a temporary autoshedder rule to prevent duplicate billing on retries: set `retry_meter_dedupe=true` on meter-service.

opsbot: runbook-created: RB-2026-0317-01 (rollback prefix_kv_cache_v2) — assigned to Jordan L., Lee C. steps logged.

Maria R.: quick note — auth-service team should revert header sanitizer change if rollback doesn't clear 401s. The sanitizer was intended to trim trailing whitespace; might be overly aggressive.

Jordan L.: executing rollback now (starting 18:25 UTC). will post completion.

opsbot: deploy-action: `config set routing.prefix_kv_cache_v2=false --env=us-west1 --author=JordanL --ticket=SUP-5412` executed at 18:26 UTC

Sam W.: monitoring — 5xx dropping from 4.3% -> 0.7% in the last 2m. p50 latency back to normal. Billing duplicate hits reduced.

Anna (support): updated SUP-5412: customer confirmed errors stopped after you paused the rollout. They've asked for postmortem and assurance their billing will be reconciled.

Lee C.: follow-ups: 1) block next deploy that mixes routing flags + auth-sanitizer in same release 2) add e2e test with long header strings 3) create a billing-dedupe check in meter pipeline 4) auth-service to review sanitizer patch.

Jordan L.: agreed. I'll open a changelist with required gating and assign owners. Also recommend a short rollback drill this week.

Sam W.: thanks team. I'll coordinate postmortem and billing reconciliation with finance/support. closing thread when postmortem link is up. :white_check_mark:
